newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-INDIA WILL COPE WITH CONDITIONS, SAYS TENDULKAR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA WILL COPE WITH CONDITIONS, SAYS TENDULKAR.

text.p: India captain Sachin Tendulkar believes his squad will have few problems adjusting to South African conditions when their 12-match tour begins in Port Elizabeth on Saturday.
The 16-player India squad flew into Johannesburg on Thursday for the start of a five-month trip which includes three tests against the South Africans then five in the West Indies.
The squad contains only six players who were in the Indian party which lost a four test series in South Africa four years ago but Tendulkar does not believe it will be a problem.
"Our newcomers are a very talented lot and we feel they are capable of handling the conditions here," he said.
"Back home in India the tracks are much slower so we rely on spinners, but the fast bowlers did an excellent job for us in the series just ended against South Africa.
"We have a very young side and that victory back home has boosted the confidence."
India won the home series against South Africa, clinching a 2-1 victory in the third test.
The first test on South African soil begins in Durban on December 26. India have only one warm-up match -- a three-ay game against Eastern Province starting on Saturday.

Sachin Tendulkar (captain), Anil Kumble (vice-captain), Mohammad Azharuddin, Pankaj Dharmani, Rahul Dravid, Doda Ganesh, Saurav Ganguly, David Johnson, Syed Saba Karim, V.V.S. Laxman, Nayan Mongia, Venkatesh Prasad, Venkatapathy Raju, Woorkeri Raman, Vikan Rathore, Javagal Srinath.
